summary: An index of the RFC series as of a date in December 1973, listing the documents published up to then so readers can find them.

eli5.summary: It is a table of contents for all the notes written so far, so you can find the one you want.

subtitle: A comprehensive directory of every RFC published through December 1973.

tldr.problem: By late 1973, over 500 RFCs had been published in the ARPANET community. Readers had no single place to find what existed or to locate a specific RFC by topic.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 598 is an index listing every published RFC with its number, title, author, date, and a brief classification. It serves as the master catalog of the series.
tldr.outcome: RFC indexes became a standard practice, published periodically. Today, the full RFC series is indexed and searchable online, descending from this early effort.

today: RFC 598 is an archival index of early ARPANET documentation. The RFC series itself continues today, now managed by the RFC Editor with over 9,000 published RFCs. Periodic indexes, now digital, remain essential for navigating the corpus.

sections.title: Organizing the RFC Series
sections.content:
By December 1973, the ARPANET and wider Internet community had published nearly 600 Requests for Comments (RFCs), each documenting a design decision, protocol specification, experimental result, or policy note. Without a comprehensive index, finding a relevant RFC was difficult.

RFC 598 compiles a complete list of all RFCs from the beginning of the series through 5 December 1973, giving each one a line with its number, title, author, date of publication, and status.
sections.eli5: By 1973, hundreds of technical notes had been shared across the network. This document is simply a list: number, title, who wrote it, and when.

sections.title: The Index as Reference Tool
sections.content:
RFC 598 serves as a reference archive and catalog. A researcher or implementer could consult the index to find all RFCs on a topic—for example, all Telnet-related documents, all file transfer work, or all policy discussions—by scanning the titles and authors. The index made the distributed nature of RFC publication transparent, showing that the community had collectively produced hundreds of specifications and analyses.

Each entry is precise: the RFC number (no longer just names), the exact title as published, author names, month and year of publication, and any relevant note about status or relation to other RFCs.
sections.eli5: It lists every note in order: the number, the exact title, who wrote it, and when. Readers can scan to find what they need.

sections.title: A Growing Practice
sections.content:
RFC 598 was not the first index—earlier indexes existed—but it became a model for a continuing practice. As the RFC series grew, new indexes were published periodically, allowing the community to track and discover work across the expanding network. The periodic RFC index became a standard part of the RFC infrastructure.

Today, the RFC Editor maintains a complete, searchable archive of all RFCs, with metadata, abstracts, and cross-references—a direct evolution of what RFC 598 started.
sections.eli5: After this, the network kept publishing a new list every year or so. Today, you can search online and find any RFC ever written.
